area: UI: the lid (centre of the core) and its wiring — ui/focus.js, ui/app.js, ui/model.js, ui/queue.js, ui/words.js, ui/api.js, ui/card.js, plus ARCHITECTURE.md "UI contract" and the UI check scripts
summary: The lid is built by a single pure-ish function, lidView(f, o) in ui/focus.js:74. It returns { key, html, say, count, idle, bind } for one focus, which currentFocus() picks in model.js:60-75 in this order: a confirm card, the picked or stepped agent, needsQueue()[0], reviewQueue()[0], then empty. app.js owns everything around it. buildLid (app.js:166-186) re-runs lidView with fit = 0..6 until the HTML measured in #probe fits maxPage (app.js:331). paintLid (238-279) patches the page when the key is unchanged and swaps it when the key changes: the old page fades for 200 ms, the new one rises for 360 ms, the answers are armed for about 760 ms, focus moves to the h1, and open{} is reset. One delegated click handler on #pages (447-536) dispatches data-act. Acts in the GUARDED set are ignored while armed. The handler then checks data-agent, data-ask and data-state against S.agents and calls changed() ("That changed. Have another look.") on any mismatch before it calls an api.js method. Finished agents get exactly two big buttons per state: done_checked/done_claimed get "Looks good" + "Ask for a change"; checks_failed gets "Ask it to fix that" + "Look later"; failed gets "Try again" + "Dismiss"; stopped gets "Continue" + "Dismiss"; earlier gets "Continue" (only when canContinue) + "Forget". Their only quiet extra is "What changed?", and only in detail 'more' at fit < 5. It toggles open.changed, which shows filesList(): the first 6 paths with +adds −dels, from a.files. The view never loads a diff. a.files is null for failed and stopped agents, and earlier agents get no link at all. Confirm cards are generic engine-worded { id, sentence, detail }. They are rendered with fixed "Do it" (primary) and "Cancel" buttons carrying data-confirm, and the detail is dropped at fit ≥ 3. Forget is the only button-started confirm: it posts the words 'forget it' with focusId to /api/command and puts r.confirm into S.confirm. Scroll boxes are the only place lid text may overflow: `.readall` ("Read all of it", from fit 4) and `code.all` ("See all of it", for a permission's command). Both are data-scroll="1" tabindex="0" with a max height of 9.5em. ui-fit-check exempts them only from vertical clipping. Nothing in the UI, the API or the engine shows a diff or merges today; ARCHITECTURE.md:103 says "the page offers no merge". The lid's inner width is 256/292/332 px (about 38-48 monospace columns at the small size) and its page is at most 344-416 px tall. A real diff therefore cannot live in the lid: it needs a read-only sheet beside the core, which has 292 px at 960 wide, 428 px at 1280, 508 px at 1440 and 718 px at 1920. Merge and Throw away must stay lid buttons in #pages, because only there do they get the guard, the id binding, busy/retry and the confirm flow.

keyFacts.fact: bigButton(label, d, pri) and quiet(label, d, extra) turn every key of d into data-* (attrs() drops null/false values) and add data-key=`${act}:${label}`, which patchChildren uses to restore focus. Big buttons are class 'big' (plus ' pri' for primary); quiet ones are class 'quiet'.

Binding objects used by every agent button: id={agent}, withAsk={agent, ask: ask.id}, st={agent, state: a.state}. Finished-state buttons all spread st, so they carry data-agent and data-state but never data-ask.

The lid key is `${a.id}|${a.state}|${ask?.id||''}` and bind is { agentId, askId }; a confirm card's key is 'confirm:'+id and its bind is { confirmId }. app.js recomputes the same key separately in keyOf(). A new sub-state that does not change a.state is therefore PATCHED, not swapped: the guard does not arm, open{} is not reset, and the data-state check still passes.

The switch runs on `a.earlier && !a.parentId ? 'earlier' : a.state`. In 'earlier' the count line says 'From an earlier run'. The sentence comes from an ended map: done_checked 'was done and checked', done_claimed 'said it was done', checks_failed 'was done, but a check failed', failed 'stopped with an error', stopped 'was stopped'. The meta lines show the time ago plus says, and the budget note or continueReason (the note only when fs.meta). Acts: Continue {act:'fix', ...st, text:'Please continue where you left off.'} (primary, only when canContinue), then Forget {act:'forget', ...st}, which is primary when it cannot continue. There is no 'What changed?'.

checks_failed: sentence '<Name> is done, but a check failed.'; meta 'failed: <names>'. Acts: 'Ask it to fix that' {act:'fix', ...st, text:'A check failed (<names>). Please fix it.'} (primary) and 'Look later' {act:'later', ...st}. With more && fs.extras it adds the 'What changed?'/'Hide the changes' toggle {act:'changed'} with aria-expanded, plus filesList when open.

done_checked/done_claimed: sentence ' is done and checked.' or ' says it is done.'. A broken rule always shows as '

One thing to know: it broke a rule you set (…)'. says is shown when fs.meta. Acts: 'Looks good' {act:'looksgood', ...st, answer:'Looks good'} (primary) and 'Ask for a change' {act:'reply', ...st, mode:'say'}. The 'What changed?' toggle only appears with more && fs.extras.

failed: '<Name> stopped with an error.' with a meta line from error/stateReason. A root gets 'Try again' {fix, text 'Please try again.'} (primary) + 'Dismiss' {act:'reviewed'}; a helper gets 'Back' {act:'parent'}. stopped: '<Name> was stopped.', with 'Continue' {fix, 'Please continue where you left off.'} + 'Dismiss'. Neither state has any quiet link about changes.

Quiet links do show in calm: 'Back to what needs me'/'Close' {act:'unpick'} for any picked agent outside a queue, 'Look at … now' on the empty lid, and the readall/exact toggles. Only 'Answer in your own words', 'Give it a hint', 'What changed?' and the spend line are gated on `more && fs.extras`.

filesList(a) shows at most 6 of a.files.list as 'path +adds −dels', marks ignored files '(hidden by a .gitignore it changed)', and adds 'and N more'. It ignores binary/large/untracked: a binary file reads '+0 −0' (verified by probe). It shows 'No files changed.' when !files.changed.

fitSteps(fit): hDown=min(3,fit); meta=2 for fit<2, 1 at fit 2, 0 from fit 3; longCut ∞ / 190 from fit 4 / 140 at fit 6; cmd 160 / 72 at fit 6; why ∞ / 60 at fit 6; extras = fit<5; tight and close from fit 5. Probe: an OPEN 'What changed?' list and its link vanish at fit 5.

Confirm card: count line 'You said'; h1 = long(c.sentence), with 'Read all of it' past longCut; detail only when fs.meta (dropped from fit 3, though it stays in say). Acts are fixed: 'Do it' {act:'confirm', confirm:id, go:'1'} (primary) and 'Cancel' {go:'0'}.

Scroll boxes: readAllBox = `<div class="readall" data-scroll="1" tabindex="0" aria-label="All of it">`. For a permission, `<code class="all" tabindex="0" data-scroll="1" aria-label="The exact command, in full">` (cmd plus why) appears when open.exact && cut. CSS caps both at max-height var(--l-allh, 9.5em) with overflow auto, which is about 7 lines.

Page-local toggles: act exact|changed|all|readall flips open[k] (readall maps to 'all'), calls renderNow() and refocuses the same [data-act]. They are not GUARDED. open = { key, exact, changed, all } is reset whenever the lid key changes.

GUARDED = answer, looksgood, fix, stop, reviewed, later, confirm, reply, parent, pick, forget. These are ignored while performance.now() < armedUntil. arm(calm ? 500 : OUT_MS+IN_MS+200) runs on every key change, and the core gets the 'arming' class.

Dispatch after the binding checks (a missing agent, a data-ask that differs from a.ask.id, or a data-state that differs from a.state all call changed()): answer → api.answer(id, ask, answer); reply → startReply (opens the input bound to agent/ask/state); fix → api.say(id, data-text); forget → api.command('forget it', {focusId}), then S.confirm = r.confirm or say(r.reply); looksgood → api.answer(id, null, 'Looks good') + markReviewed; reviewed → markReviewed only; later → setAside; stop → api.stop; parent → S.focusId = parentId. Then moved() and render(). On error: retry(b) + say(err.message). Sending acts use busy(b), which hands focus to the h1.

The confirm button path checks S.confirm.id === data-confirm (else changed()), then busy, api.confirm(id, go==='1'), clears S.confirm, say(r.reply), lookAt(r.focusId), moved(). dropConfirm() (Esc, or picking a chip) posts go:false and puts the card back if that fails.

Holding: engaged() is true while the pointer is in the core, focus is inside the core (not the input), the input has text, voice is listening, or S.reply is open. It turns false after 20 s with no input unless listening or text is typed. shownFocus() keeps the held item and sets also → '

Another one needs you'. Own moves call moved(), so letGo skips the hold once.

Typed or spoken words bind to lastView.bind, taken at the first keystroke. bindingNow() returns {} while armed or while an old or hidden page exists. With a done agent on screen, text goes to /api/command { text, focusId: agent, askId: null }.

Global keys: ←/→ step the queue unless focus is a control or inside #look; any printable key is moved into the input unless focus is inside #look; Space is hold-to-talk unless a control has focus ([tabindex="0"] counts as a control). mousedown on any button is preventDefault'ed, so clicks never move focus. escape() order: look, pop, trayList, voice, reply, input blur, pin, confirm, then focus the h1.

Overlay pattern (tray list): width room = G.core.x - 12 - (G.board.x + 8); top = G.board.y + P.topBand; maxHeight up to the anchor; never on the core. Outside clicks close #pop, #trayList and #look. Measured room beside the core: 292px at 960x900 (S), 324 at 1024x700, 428 at 1280x680 (M), 508 at 1440x789, 514 at 1512x862 (L), 622 at 1728, 718 at 1920, 1038 at 2560. That is about 41/46/62/74/72/87/101/148 columns at the small mono size; the lid's inner width is only 256/292/332 px (38/44/48 columns).

S.meta.repo = { name, head, branch, dirty } is set ONLY in onSnapshot (on connect, and after a forget's 'removed'). The engine refreshes repoInfo on its 1 s tick every repoEveryMs but never pushes it, so a branch label on the page can be stale. branch is null on a detached HEAD.

reviewQueue = roots, not earlier, state in done_checked|done_claimed|failed, not in S.reviewed (sessionStorage 'wb-reviewed', keyed by finishKey = `${id}@${endedAt??stateSince??0}`), newest first. stopped is never 'to look at'; checks_failed is in needsQueue unless set aside. These marks are per tab.

api.js: call() throws RequestError(plainError) on non-2xx, calls onRefused on 401, and throws a refused Error(reply) on {ok:false} with status 200. The api object has exactly: state, command(text,{focusId,confirmId,askId}), confirm(id,go), answer(agentId, askId, answer) (askId omitted when null), say, stop, awake. GET sends the token in a header, never the URL.

AgentView.files = { changed, adds, dels, list:[{path, adds, dels, binary?, large?, untracked?, ignored?}] } | null. AgentView.workspace is a PATH STRING only; branch and base live in the engine's run.workspace and the history record.

files exists only after a receipt: a turn ending isError returns before diffStats, _stop cancels the receipt, and a new turn clears files. So failed and stopped agents have files=null even when their folder holds work, and a done agent's files can go stale if the folder is edited later. diffStats compares the WORKTREE to base, including uncommitted, untracked and ignored-but-hidden files.

Engine confirm records are { id, kind, …, sentence, detail, createdAt } with a 10-minute TTL. _confirm dispatches on kind (forget/stop/say/launch), and confirmVerb gives the 'Say “do it” to …' wording. Forget's card: 'Forget <Name>?' with detail 'It will not show here again. Its folder and branch stay on this computer.'
'Looks good' on a done agent changes nothing in the engine: 'Good. <Name> stays as it is.'

commands.mjs WORK_VERBS includes merge, delete, remove, review, commit, revert, undo, restore, push. So typed or spoken 'merge it', 'review it' or 'delete it' with a finished agent on screen becomes a launch confirm for a NEW agent today.

ui-fit-check exempts [data-scroll] only VERTICALLY: lines 67 and 76 clamp top and bottom, never left and right. A horizontally scrolling diff line therefore fails as 'text outside its box' or 'off-screen text'. Text layers are hard-coded as '#card, #pop, #trayList, #look'; the overlay rule (never on the core or top band) is hard-coded to the same four ids. The VIEWS list has no review or merge view.

The mock API has no diff, merge or discard routes. view() hard-codes workspace:null; world() sets mode 'demo' and repo null (only the 'live' scenario has repo {branch:'main', dirty:3}). Confirm handling knows launch and forget only.

Test conventions: the lid tests map /shared/ with module.registerHooks and use buttons(html) to parse data-*. The binding test loops STATES_ALL × calm/more and asserts that every non-local act carries data-agent; the page-local skip-list is ['next','exact','changed','readall','unpick']. Earlier-agent lid tests are in ui-history.test.mjs.
The behaviour-check's own-move tests use 'Looks good' in the alldone scenario, and Forget/Continue is the template for a confirm-first flow (posts checked via /ctl/log).

Contract text: 'the page offers no merge'; Forget never touches the worktree or branch; the Answers table lists every button → request pair; /say and /stop carry no ask id, so buttons must carry data-state; overlays never cover the core or the top band; text ≥ 10.5 px; contrast 4.5:1 for text and 3:1 for marks.

Server: POST needs JSON, at most 64 KB, and a same-origin Origin; the routes table has no diff, merge or discard routes; the CSP is default-src 'self' (no inline scripts or handlers; inline style is allowed).

rulesToHonour: At most two big answer buttons in the lid. The first is primary, except where equal weight is required (Allow/Deny, and should be Throw away). Labels never wrap: buttonRow() goes side by side, then 'tight', then 'stack' (words.js:42-48). A long branch name must be clipped inside the label (clipMiddle), with the full name in title/aria-label and in the confirm card.

Every button carries what it was drawn for: data-agent, data-ask when there is an ask, and data-state for anything sent without an ask id. app.js re-checks each against S.agents before sending and otherwise says 'That changed. Have another look.' and redraws. New acts must also carry and check what they bind to (target branch, finishKey or diff id).

Acts that send something or move the lid go in GUARDED (ignored for about 760 ms after a swap). They live in #pages, whose single click handler provides the guard, busy()/retry() and the binding checks; buttons outside #pages get none of this.
Any new lid sub-state must change the lid key in BOTH focus.js:286 and app.js:122 keyOf(); otherwise it is patched in place, with no fade, no guard and no reset of open{}.

Anything that starts agents, and any act whose words did not name the agent, goes through an engine-worded confirm card ({id, sentence, detail}). Cards are bound by id and expire after 10 minutes. The page withdraws a dropped card with POST /api/confirm/<id> {go:false} (on Esc or a pick) and keeps the card if that post fails. A typed 'yes' carries confirmId.

Refusals arrive as {ok:false, reply} with status 200: show the reply, redraw from the current state, and leave the request waiting. A failed answer is not a move: the lid stays held and the button is re-enabled with focus returned to it.

Calm shows one sentence, a short meta line, at most two answers and the input. Quiet extras are for 'more', except where 'security over calm' applies: a permission's exact command and reason, the readall/exact toggles and unpick also show in calm. A way to see what would land before a merge belongs in that exception class.

Fit ladder order (fitSteps): headline smaller, meta shortened, meta dropped, long texts cut at 190 with 'Read all of it', then tighter buttons, closer command and no extras, and finally the last-resort cuts. Security-relevant text survives to the last step, and every new element needs a defined place in this ladder.

Holding: while the person is busy with the core, stream changes do not swap the lid; 'Another one needs you' shows instead. The person's own moves (lid buttons, picks, replies to their own command) always show at once through moved().

Focus: never move focus onto an answer button. When the lid's item changes, focus that was in the lid goes to its h1 (tabindex=-1). busy() hands focus to the h1 and retry() gives it back. Keyboard focus is never dropped, and Esc returns focus to whatever opened the overlay.

Overlays stay inside the window and never cover the core or the top band (fit-check rule 5). Scroll boxes are data-scroll="1" tabindex="0" with an aria-label, and are exempt from VERTICAL clipping only. Text is at least 10.5 px; contrast is 4.5:1 for text and 3:1 for marks and lines, in all three looks; every state has its own mark and colour only repeats it.

Plain language everywhere: sentences, not identifiers; never 'token' or 'fetch'; no percentages or estimated finish times; counters in whole minutes. Everything an agent controls (diff text, paths, branch names, says) goes through esc(), and control characters are made visible (visibleControls).

Pure modules (queue.js, words.js, util.js and any new diffview.js) touch no DOM when they load and import nothing from /shared/. Tests live in test/ui-*.test.mjs (focus.js tests use the registerHooks /shared/ mapping), use node:test, never use the network, and never start a real claude or codex.

CSP default-src 'self': no inline scripts or event handlers (all listeners are delegated from app.js); inline style is allowed. POSTs are JSON, at most 64 KB, same Origin. The page sends the token only in a header (the stream URL is the one exception).

The contract and the code must agree: ARCHITECTURE.md (including 'the page offers no merge', the Answers table and the fit-check views) is updated in the same change. Builders edit only their own area's files.
risks: The branch name can be stale. S.meta.repo.branch changes only on a snapshot, although the engine refreshes repoInfo on its tick. A 'Merge into main' label can name the branch the person has since left. The button must carry data-branch, and the engine must re-check it and name the live branch in its confirm; better, push repo changes to the page. A detached HEAD (branch null) needs its own words and no Merge button.

Lid-key trap: a merge outcome that keeps a.state (merged, conflict, blocked) gives the same key, so the page is patched silently, the guard does not arm, and the old Merge button's data-state check still passes.
Buttons placed in a diff sheet or any overlay bypass GUARDED, armedUntil, busy/retry and the binding checks. Keep the sheet read-only, or give it its own guard and binding.

The fit-check fails horizontally scrolling diff lines: the [data-scroll] exemption is vertical only (ui-fit-check.mjs:67, 76). It also hard-codes the text layers and the overlay list, so a new #review overlay would raise 'text on text' failures against chips beneath it unless it is added at lines 65 and 132.

There is very little room. The lid's inner width is 256-332 px (about 38-48 columns), and the scroll box holds about 7 lines (9.5em). The side sheet is only 292 px at 960 wide and 324 px at 1024 (about 41-46 columns), so the diff must wrap at small sizes.

'What changed?' appears only in 'more' and vanishes at fit ≥ 5, even when open (extras = fit < 5). Calm has no way to see changes. If Review stays an 'extra', a Merge button would be offered with no way to look at the work in small windows.

The confirm card is unfit for destructive acts as it stands: detail is hidden at fit ≥ 3; 'Do it' is the primary (dark default) button; labels are fixed; the count says 'You said' even for button-started cards. A typed or misheard spoken 'yes' settles any card shown.

Refusals and outcomes shown only through say() last 9 s and 3 lines (5 s for 'That changed'). A conflict, or 'your uncommitted changes are in the way', needs a persistent lid state backed by a server field.

The data is incomplete or stale. files is null for failed and stopped agents (failed returns before diffStats; stop cancels the receipt) and is cleared at each new turn. A done agent's files is a snapshot taken at turn end, and an earlier agent's comes from history. The diff must be fetched on demand, and merge must be bound to the diff id the person actually saw.

What the lid lists may not be what a merge lands. diffStats counts uncommitted, untracked and ignored-but-hidden files, and README.md:119 says the changes may not be committed. The lid and confirm wording must not promise more, or less, than the engine commits and merges.
filesList shows binary files as '+0 −0' and ignores the large and untracked flags, which misleads anyone about to merge.

Typed or spoken 'merge it', 'review it', 'delete it', 'undo' or 'revert' are WORK_VERBS today. With a finished agent on screen they produce a launch confirm for a new agent. Until the parser gains intents, the buttons are the only safe path; say so if the page hints at words.

Holding versus reading. engaged() ignores a sheet outside the core and lets go after 20 s idle, so the lid can swap under someone reading a diff. The global ←/→ keys step the queue, and printable keys jump to the input, unless the sheet is excluded the way #look is.
Review-queue marks (wb-reviewed, wb-later) are per-tab sessionStorage. A merged or thrown-away agent must leave the queue by server state, or a second tab offers to merge it again.

Rendering big diffs: unbounded DOM, and agent-controlled content (HTML, bidi or 'Trojan Source' characters, CR, tabs). The engine must cap; the page must escape everything and show invisible characters. visibleControls covers only C0 and DEL, not U+202A-202E, U+2066-2069 or zero-width characters.

Demo and mock have no worktrees: workspace is null, repo is null and mode is 'demo'. Merge needs an explicit condition field, or the buttons will show in demo and fail. The behaviour-check's 'Looks good' own-move tests (alldone) break if that button is replaced.

Merging into the person's checkout can leave it mid-merge (conflict markers, a MERGING state) or overwrite edits. The UI must never call that a success, and it needs words for a half-done merge, if the engine allows one. (This is the engine's design, but it drives the lid.)
openQuestions: Should 'merged' be a new STATE, with a LOOK mark, PRIORITY and set membership in states.mjs (touching look.js, boardmodel, card, queue and the contrast pairs)? Or a field such as merge: {state, into, at} on a done state?
Is 'Looks good' replaced by 'Merge into <branch>', or kept as a quiet 'Not now' or 'Keep it without merging'? How does a person keep work unmerged and stop being shown it, in calm?

Should Merge always go through an engine-worded confirm card? (Recommended: it names the live branch and what moved.) Or only when something is unusual: a moved branch, a dirty checkout, a failed check?
Which states offer Merge: done_checked and done_claimed only? checks_failed as 'Merge anyway' in more? failed or stopped (partial work)? Earlier agents whose folder still exists?

Must a review come before a merge? This choice is between a stricter two-step (lid offers 'Review the changes' first, then 'Merge' once that diff id has been seen, with a key change) and Merge always available beside a Review link.

Is the diff sheet a side overlay beside the core (keeps the lid visible, 292-1038 px wide, covers chips like the card or tray do), or a full-window review mode? The latter would change the 'overlays never on the core' rule and the holding logic.
Should diff lines wrap (works with the fit-check as written), or scroll horizontally (needs the fit-check to clamp [data-scroll] horizontally too)?
Does Throw away accept a typed or spoken 'yes', or only the button and explicit words ('throw it away')? Does it also forget the agent in history, or keep a 'thrown away' record?
After a successful merge, should the agent's folder and branch be removed automatically (safe once merged and clean), or offered as 'Remove its folder'?
If the agent's work in its folder is uncommitted, does the merge commit it (with what message and author), and does the review show exactly that commit?
How does the page learn the person's current branch and its dirty state in time: a pushed snapshot, a new 'repo' SSE event, or only the confirm card's words?
In demo mode, should merge and throw-away be simulated, so the flow can be shown and fit-checked without git? Or hidden?
Should button-started confirm cards (Forget, Merge, Throw away) get a different count line than 'You said', for example via a kind field on the confirm payload?
